verdicts.reason: Both use the same broken banner template. The dark header band is a stray rectangle in the top-right, the white SOLSTICE wordmark nearly disappears on cream, the orange divider is stranded on the right, the 'Limited Summer Release' eyebrow now sits below the body copy, and the CTA is tiny with its label barely readable. A's CTA sits slightly further in from the left edge and its legal block is a little tighter. B's button is shoved further left and its legal text runs wider.

These are effectively the same layout. Both have the orphaned dark rectangle top-right, a wordmark you can't read, a stranded divider, the eyebrow moved below the body copy, an undersized CTA and illegible legal text right next to the button. A's legal text fits on two lines and B's wraps a third line ('details.'), but neither difference matters.

A has the usual flaws: stray dark rectangle, invisible wordmark, eyebrow out of order, tiny CTA, legal text crammed beside the button. It is still readable and uses the banner width. B is just the portrait original shrunk into a thin centre strip. Every line of text is microscopic, and over 60% of the canvas is empty on each side, so it is unusable.

A shares the template flaws: orphaned dark rectangle, unreadable wordmark, eyebrow placed below the body copy, undersized CTA. Its headline and body copy still wrap cleanly. In B the headline wraps and leaves 'Yet' alone on a line, the body copy ends on the orphan 'solstice.' crammed against the CTA, the eyebrow shrinks to a tiny label beside the button, and the legal text floats as an unrelated column on the right, which makes the layout ragged and lopsided.
